OpenEval notes contradiction with prior literature; peer reviewers accepted findings with only minor figure labeling corrections requested.

Divergent evaluations with 100% claim overlap (C126-C133). OpenEval finds sequential stimulation experiments well-supported with appropriate design. Peer reviewers marked UNCERTAIN, noting 'confusion has to do with the order of engagement' and requesting additional timing experiments.

Divergent evaluations with 100% claim overlap (C134-C142). OpenEval finds TLR-deficiency experiments strongly support B-1 cell-intrinsic requirement. Peer reviewers marked UNCERTAIN, requesting clarification on 'B cell-intrinsic nature of TLR signaling' and coordination with companion paper.

Strong agreement with 71.4% claim overlap (C80-C88, C93). Both support neonatal chimera findings showing CD5+ to CD5- conversion. OpenEval emphasizes elegant experimental design; peer reviewers praised chimera approach but requested additional CD5- transfer controls.

Agreement on BCR reorganization with 50% claim overlap (C121-C125). Both support temporal analysis showing BCR complex changes precede CD5 transcriptional changes. OpenEval highlights multiple complementary readouts; peer reviewers accepted findings as supporting the integration mechanism.

Divergent evaluations with 47.4% claim overlap (C102-C104, C110-C115). OpenEval finds PLA data provide direct molecular evidence for BCR signalosome interactions. Peer reviewers marked UNCERTAIN, questioning 'how can CD5 be detected in the PLA in CD5- B1 cells?' and finding data 'difficult to interpret.'

Agreement on control experiments with 42.9% claim overlap (C62-C67). Both support findings addressing alternative explanations for CD5 loss. OpenEval emphasizes rigorous controls; peer reviewers initially requested clarification on experimental purpose but would likely accept after explanation.

Strong agreement with 36.4% claim overlap (C75-C77, C79). Both support TLR-dependent CD5 loss and differentiation findings. OpenEval highlights TLR-deficient mice as strong evidence; peer reviewers found this 'exciting' and noted it 'requests reconsideration for interpretation of previous studies.'

Agreement on B-1 vs B-2 comparisons with 35.7% claim overlap (C105-C109). Both support comparative findings showing B-1-specific mechanisms. OpenEval notes functional evidence for non-proliferation; peer reviewers accepted data as supporting integration of innate and adaptive stimuli.

Strong agreement with 30% claim overlap (C69-C74). Both support in vitro TLR-induced CD5 downregulation. OpenEval emphasizes flow cytometry and qRT-PCR evidence; peer reviewers found demonstration 'convincing' and experiments 'elegant.'

Agreement on differentiation model with 28.6% claim overlap (C89-C92). Both support CD5+ to CD5- differentiation in lymph nodes. OpenEval highlights BrdU incorporation and correlation analysis; peer reviewers accepted findings without specific critique, though requested body cavity analysis as additional data.

Partial overlap with 26.3% shared claims (C116-C120). OpenEval supports BCR signaling readouts showing reorganization precedes CD5 changes. Peer reviewers' UNCERTAIN evaluation of PLA data (R5) may extend to these related claims, though phospho-flow and Nur77 data were not specifically critiqued.

Strong agreement with 26.1% claim overlap (C55-C59, C68). Both support in vitro CD5 downregulation and temporal kinetics. OpenEval emphasizes comprehensive controls; peer reviewers found in vitro demonstration 'convincing' and praised experimental quality.

Agreement on main conclusions with 17.6% claim overlap (C5-C7). OpenEval finds abstract claims well-supported by comprehensive evidence. Peer reviewers' positive evaluation of core findings (R1) implicitly supports these summary conclusions about TLR-induced CD5 loss.
